seatRig.description: The authored chase framing, or null for a document that seats no body; SeatRig is what a reader resolves through.

seatControl.description: The authored constraints for live seat camera input, or null for a document that seats no body; SeatControl is what a reader resolves through.

yawReference.description: What the camera yaw is relative to.
yawReference.title: WorldSeatYawReference

minPitch.description: The minimum live pitch offset in radians.

maxPitch.description: The maximum live pitch offset in radians.

follow.description: The follow camera: with no look input the camera yaw eases in behind the body's heading; any look input (a deflected look stick, a held orbit/steer) is free-look and the follow yields for as long as it lasts. Optional; absent is a still camera that goes only where look input sends it. Needs World — a body-relative yaw already rides the body.

rate.description: The exponential rate (per second) the camera yaw closes on the heading — about 63% of the remaining angle per 1/rate seconds; larger is a stiffer follow.

whileIdle.description: Whether the follow also runs while the body has no movement input. false (the default) is the classic feel: after a free-look the camera stays where you left it until you move.

follow.title: WorldSeatFollow

seatControl.title: WorldSeatViewControl

cameraRig.description: The program a seat's view resolves through while its published mode state targets CameraTarget — null for a world that authors no camera-targeting mode state. Resolved through the ordinary Puck.World.Client.WorldCameraRigCompiler pipeline against whichever body the seat currently perceives from (the possessed camera body — see Puck.World.Server.WorldEngagement), exactly like SeatRig resolves against the seat's own avatar; no bespoke per-frame integrator reads this field.

shaderToolchain.description: The directory holding the graph compiler's dxc, or null to resolve it by bare name through the ordinary executable search path — never an environment variable.

graphs.description: The authored views.graphs frame-graph instances (empty = none declared).

items.description: One named instance of a frame graph: a view rendered by a puck.render.graph.v1 document, such as a pane, a game camera shown on a screen, or a nested world, or an engine package's producer such as the SDF world. A Instance shows it in a layout, and the pipeline.* console verbs address it by name. The row carries authored intent; planning, scheduling, compilation and resources belong to the renderer.

name.description: The instance's stable name (a SafeName, unique within the section), which another row's input, a layout slot and a capture name.

source.description: Where the instance's graph comes from, or null for a row that names a Package: a puck.render.graph.v1 graph document, a one-off shader source file, which reads as a one-pass graph, or a puck.shader.package.v1 package directory, which loads with its source tree gone. It resolves beside the document that authors it (WorldDocumentPaths), like every relative path a document authors.

package.description: The engine package whose producer renders the instance, such as sdf.world, or null for a row that names a Source. A package instance reads no input and takes no time scale, output or override.

camera.description: The authored camera the instance renders from, feeding the frame block's cameraPosition, cameraTarget, cameraUp and cameraFov, or null, which leaves cameraFov zero so a graph keeps its own pointer orbit.

refresh.description: How often it refreshes, or null for every frame something visible reads it.

divisor.description: The instance renders at most once every this many presented frames, or null when Hertz states the rate.

hertz.description: The most renders a second, or null when Divisor states the rate.

refresh.title: WorldViewGraphRefresh

inputs.description: The external versions of its graph bound to other instances' outputs, or null for none.

items.description: One external version of a graph instance's document bound to another instance's output.

resource.description: The external version of the instance's graph document the binding fills.

instance.description: The views.graphs row whose output fills it. Naming the row's own instance reads its previous frame.

previousFrame.description: Whether the read takes the producer's previous completed frame, which lets two instances show each other. Default false: the producer renders first in the same frame.

items.title: WorldViewGraphInput

timeScale.description: The instance clock's rate multiplier — presentation only, never simulation state. Default 1; 0 freezes the clock.

output.description: The image version the instance shows, or null for the source's first declared output.

overrides.description: This instance's parameter overrides, keyed by pass name; each value is that pass's config object keyed by field. A field absent here keeps the default the shared source declares, so two instances of one source differ only in what they override. The source's config schema binds them when a boot, a world.load or world.reload, a commit, or an upsert names them (the server reads the source, and refuses a value by name), and again when a graph installs (the host binds them into its passes). null overrides nothing.

additionalProperties.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

items.title: WorldViewGraph

graphBudget.description: The graph scheduler's price ceiling, or null for none.

passPixelsPerFrame.description: The pass-pixels (passes times rendered pixels) those instances may spend in one presented frame; the stalest due instance is admitted first and the rest read their latest completed output. 0 sets no ceiling.

graphBudget.title: WorldViewGraphBudget

root.description: The views.graphs row the display shows and captures read, or null for the render graph composition synthesizes from the document around WorldViewGraphs.WorldInstance and WorldViewGraphs.MainInstance. A world that names its root authors its whole render graph, the sdf.world package row included.

layouts.description: Gets the authored named layouts. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

items.description: One named window composition — an ordered list of WorldViewSlots plus a transition envelope, selected for a given session shape by its SeatCount (0 = the catch-all for any joined-seat count). The data-side replacement for a compiled layout switch: an author can see it, change it, and add arrangements.

name.description: The layout's stable name (the view.override layout override handle; unique within the section).

seatCount.description: The joined-seat count this layout composes for, or 0 for the catch-all. Default 0.

transitionSeconds.description: How long the ease into this composition takes when it becomes active. Default 0, a cut.

transitionRenderScale.description: The render scale (0, 1] applied to every slot mid-transition (a soft dip that sharpens on settle). Default 1, no dip.

slots.description: Gets the slots, in order. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

items.description: One slot of a WorldViewLayout — a normalized rect (origin top-left, Y down) plus what fills it. A slot whose Camera and Instance are both null shows the seat that owns this slot (the next joined seat in slot order); a named camera renders that authored view into the rect; a named graph instance (a WorldViewGraph row) shows its selected image output in the rect, placed over the SDF world by the render graph's root — a slot names at most one of the two (the validator refuses both authored together).

x.description: The rect's left edge, normalized [0, 1]. Default 0.

y.description: The rect's top edge, normalized [0, 1]. Default 0.

width.description: The rect's width, normalized (0, 1]. Default 1, so a slot that authors no rect fills the window.

camera.description: The authored camera name filling this slot, or null for the seat that owns it (or the instance named by Instance).

instance.description: The views.graphs row name whose output fills this slot, or null for a seat or camera slot.

items.title: WorldViewSlot
WorldViewLayout
